verdict: Ameriprise's net revenues rose 7% to $5.12B on strong advice fees, and net income rose 23% to $1.13B (EPS $12.32), helped by smaller market-related insurance charges.

segments.name: Management & financial advice fees
segments.note: Fees for financial advice and managing client money — the engine of the business, up 15% as client assets grew.

segments.name: Net investment income
segments.note: Income on the company's own investments, shown after $74M of banking and deposit interest expense (the gross figure was $908M, down 1%).

segments.name: Distribution fees
segments.note: Fees for distributing funds and products.

segments.name: Premiums & policy charges
segments.note: Insurance and annuity premiums and charges — down as the company steers away from some guarantee-heavy products.

segments.name: Other revenues
segments.note: Everything else, flat vs a year ago.

opex.name: Insurance benefits, claims & policy costs
opex.note: Benefits and claims paid ($302M), interest credited to fixed accounts ($72M), reserve changes ($234M) and deferred acquisition cost amortization ($62M).

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Staff, technology and running the firm.

takeaways.title: Net revenues rose to $5.12B
takeaways.text: Advice and management fees jumped 15% as client assets grew 12%, more than offsetting a 28% drop in insurance premiums.

takeaways.title: Net income rose to $1.13B
takeaways.text: Profit grew much faster than revenue because market-related insurance charges shrank — the change in fair value of market risk benefits fell from $302M to $202M.

takeaways.title: EPS of $12.32, up from $9.33
takeaways.text: Buybacks amplify the growth: Ameriprise has shrunk its share count from about 98M to 91M diluted shares in a year.

footerNote: Revenue is total net revenues — total revenues of $5,191M less $74M of banking and deposit interest expense, which is netted against investment income above. Distribution expenses (largely commissions paid to advisors) are treated as the direct cost of revenue. Ameriprise reports pre-tax income directly, so operating income here equals pre-tax income and there is no separate other-income line; its business segments on an adjusted basis were Advice & Wealth Management ($3,371M), Asset Management ($990M) and Retirement & Protection ($997M), before corporate and eliminations.
